mainTopic: The גר's conversion קרבן, and the new משנה on קרבנות brought even for deliberate sins and one קרבן for many sins
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of the קרבן a גר brings when he converts. It must be an offering with blood, not a מנחה. According to רבי, the גר enters the ברית just as our ancestors did: through מילה, טבילה, and sprinkling of blood. The גמרא shows that birds must come as a pair, and finds verses for each of the three steps. It also proves that גרים are accepted even today without a קרבן, and rules like רבי שמעון that a גר today does not set aside money for his birds. Another version places that ruling on a ברייתא about a גר תושב doing work on שבת. Then a new משנה lists cases where a קרבן is brought even for a deliberate sin: שפחה חרופה, a נזיר who became טמא, שבועת העדות, and שבועת הפקדון. The גמרא finds a source for each case. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that relations with five different שפחות need five קרבנות, because they are separate bodies. His proof from the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A flour offering does not count for a convert
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a גר could bring a מנחה, and rules it out from the word 'כן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I would include even a flour offering as an option. That is why the verse says 'so' (כן), to exclude it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is continuing its list of what a גר may bring as his conversion קרבן, and it now rules out a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא allowed certain offerings for the גר. Now it raises the idea that a מנחה might also be allowed, since it also goes on the מזבח. The word 'כן' in the פסוק limits the options and excludes the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' — introduces an idea that will be rejected
Include (in the law)
A flour offering (not an animal or bird)
'The verse teaches' — introduces the source that settles the question

phrases.english: One might think that I include even a meal offering?
The verse states: "So."
phrases.notes: From במדבר 15:14, 'as you do, so he shall do.' The word 'so' limits what counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section about the convert's offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה does not fulfill the גר's obligation to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: A second teaching: maybe anything burned on the altar counts
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא quotes the פסוק about a 'fire offering' and suggests that even a מנחה might count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'And he will offer a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to ה׳.' From this I would think anything that goes up on the altar fires counts, even a flour offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that starts by suggesting a broad reading of the פסוק. This sets up the next step, where the ברייתא narrows it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'fire offering' sound general, as if any קרבן burned on the מזבח would work. A מנחה is also burned on the fire, so it seems to fit. The ברייתא raises this only to reject it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire offering — something burned on the מזבח
A pleasing aroma (to ה׳)
The fires of the מזבח
'I would understand' — a first, too-broad reading

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
"And he will offer a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:14

phrases.english: I would understand anything that goes up on the altar fires,
even a meal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: שומע אני כל שעולה לאשים אפילו מנחה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא that reaches the same conclusion as step 1 from a fuller reading of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does any offering burned on the altar, even a מנחה, count for the גר?

steps.title: The convert must bring a blood offering, like you did
steps.stepSummary: From 'as you do, so he shall do,' the ברייתא learns that the גר must bring a קרבן whose blood is sprinkled, just like the Jewish people did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'As you do, so he shall do.' Just as you entered with kinds of blood offerings, so too they must bring kinds of blood offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question: a מנחה does not count, because the גר must bring the same kind of offering the Jewish people brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the גר to the Jewish people at הר סיני. They entered the ברית with animal offerings whose blood was sprinkled. So the גר also needs an offering with blood, and a מנחה has no blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As you do, so he shall do' — the פסוק comparing the גר to the Jewish people
Kinds of blood offerings — קרבנות whose blood is put on the מזבח

phrases.english: The verse states: "As you do, so he shall do" —
phrases.notes: Also from במדבר 15:14.

phrases.english: just as you brought kinds of blood offerings,
phrases.notes: 'You' means the Jewish people when they entered the covenant at Sinai.

phrases.english: so too they must bring kinds of blood offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר כאשר תעשו כן יעשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by narrowing the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a blood offering counts, because the גר is compared to the Jewish people, who entered with blood offerings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: the גר's קרבן must be a type whose blood is sprinkled, which is why a bird or animal works and flour does not.

steps.title: Then must he bring exactly an עולה and שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes the comparison further: if the גר must be like the Jewish people, he should need both an עולה and a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as you brought an עולה and a שלמים, they too should have to bring an עולה and a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own comparison: if the גר is compared to the Jewish people, why not demand the exact same offerings they brought?
steps.deeperAnalysis: At הר סיני the Jewish people brought both an עולה and שלמים. If the comparison is complete, the גר should need both too. That would rule out bringing just one עולה or birds, which the ברייתא allows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so' — introduces a challenge that pushes a comparison further
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
A peace offering, partly eaten by the owners

phrases.english: If so: just as you brought a burnt offering and a peace offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: אי מה אתם עולה ושלמים אף הם עולה ושלמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison in step 3 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison 'as you do, so he shall do' from step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גר is fully compared to the Jewish people, he should need the identical offerings: both an עולה and שלמים.

steps.title: The comparison is limited, not about the exact offerings
steps.stepSummary: From 'as you are, so shall the גר be,' the ברייתא learns the comparison is only for the type of offering, not the exact same offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse states: 'As you are, so shall the convert be.' I compared him to you, but not for another matter, meaning not to make his offerings identical to yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge: the comparison is limited, so the גר does not need both an עולה and שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra wording 'ככם כגר' shows the comparison is meant only to teach that the גר needs a blood offering. It does not stretch to copying every detail of the offerings brought at הר סיני. So one עולה or a pair of birds is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As you are, so shall the גר be'
'I compared him' — a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison made by the פסוק
Another matter — something beyond the limited point of the comparison

steps.whatToRemember: The גר must bring a blood offering, like the Jewish people did, but he does not need the exact same עולה and שלמים they brought.

phrases.english: The verse states: "As you are, so shall the convert be" —

phrases.english: I compared him to you,

phrases.notes: He means: the comparison doesn't make his offerings match yours exactly.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר ככם כגר יהיה לכם הקשתיו ולא לדבר אחר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the comparison from the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גר is compared to the Jewish people in every detail, so he needs both an עולה and שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison only requires a blood offering, not the identical offerings.

steps.title: רבי: the convert enters the covenant like our ancestors did
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads 'ככם' as 'like your ancestors,' who entered the ברית through מילה, טבילה, and sprinkling of blood, so the גר must do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: 'As you' means 'like your ancestors.' Just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision, immersion, and sprinkling of blood, so too converts can enter the covenant only through circumcision, immersion, and sprinkling of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different way of learning the גר's קרבן from the same פסוק, linking it to how our ancestors entered the ברית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of comparing the גר's offering to the offerings at Sinai, רבי compares the whole process of entering the ברית. Our ancestors needed three things: מילה, טבילה, and blood on the מזבח. So the גר also needs a קרבן with blood as one of the three steps of conversion.

keyTerms.meaning: Like your ancestors
The covenant between ה׳ and the Jewish people
Circumcision
Immersion in a מקוה
Sprinkling of blood on the מזבח, which makes the offering accepted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that conversion needs three parts: מילה, טבילה, and a קרבן with blood.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, the גר enters the ברית exactly like our ancestors: מילה, טבילה, and the sprinkling of blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: "As you" — means like your ancestors.
Just as your ancestors did not enter the covenant
except through circumcision, immersion, and the sprinkling of blood —
so too they may not enter the covenant
except through circumcision, immersion, and the sprinkling of blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק used in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר enters the ברית only through מילה, טבילה, and the sprinkling of blood from a קרבן, just as our ancestors did.

steps.title: A single bird is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that a גר cannot bring just one bird, because the Torah never has a one-bird offering. The pair of birds (קן) was only allowed to make things easier for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bringing one young bird is impossible, because we never find that anywhere in the Torah. The Torah allowed a pair of birds only to make it easier for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its rule about the גר's קרבן: if he brings birds, he must bring two, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גר has to bring a קרבן whose blood is sprinkled. Birds are a cheaper choice, but the Torah never has an offering of a single bird. So the bird choice means a pair (קן), and that choice exists only as a leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: A single young bird
A 'nest': a pair of birds brought as offerings
To make it easier for him

phrases.english: To bring one young bird – is impossible,
for we have not found this in the entire Torah.
They did not mention a nest
phrases.notes: A 'nest' means a pair of birds. Here that is the cheaper option for the גר instead of an animal.

phrases.english: except to make it easier for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי, explaining what counts as an acceptable bird offering for the גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר who brings birds must bring two. A single bird is never a complete offering in the Torah.

steps.title: Challenge: a single bird burnt offering does exist
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the Torah never has a one-bird offering. It quotes a ברייתא that lets someone pledge an עולת העוף of just one bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? A ברייתא teaches that the singular word 'and he shall sacrifice it' shows that a person who pledges a bird burnt offering may bring even one bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 7 by showing a case where one bird is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the Torah never has a one-bird offering. But the ברייתא reads the singular 'והקריבו' to teach that a voluntary bird עולה can be just one bird. That seems to prove the opposite of Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering made of a bird
Doves

phrases.english: And not?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really true that we never find a one-bird offering?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "And he shall sacrifice it",

phrases.english: why does the verse say this?
Since it says about doves: "And he shall sacrifice",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:14. That verse speaks of doves in the plural.

phrases.english: I would understand that one who says:
"It is upon me to bring a bird burnt offering"
may not bring fewer than two young birds?
The verse says: "And he shall sacrifice it" –
even one young bird!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual claim in Step 7 that a one-bird offering is never found.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement 'שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה' from Step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows a single-bird עולה, so a one-bird offering does exist in the Torah.

steps.title: Answer: no required offering is a single bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the single-bird case is voluntary. A required one-bird offering is never found.
steps.simpleTranslation: At any rate, we have not found a required offering of just one bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule from Step 7 so the challenge no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-bird עולה is a pledge someone takes on by choice. The גר's קרבן is a requirement, and among required offerings there is never a single bird. So Step 7 still stands for required offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: A required offering, not a voluntary one
At any rate
We have found

phrases.english: An obligatory offering, at any rate, we have not found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by limiting the rule to required offerings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original statement (voluntary versus required)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 7 seemed to mean that no offering of any kind is ever a single bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: Step 7 means that no required offering is a single bird. The voluntary עולה does not count.

steps.title: Challenge: the יולדת brings one bird as a required offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the narrowed rule. A woman after childbirth is required to bring a single bird as a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the woman after childbirth, who brings one young pigeon or dove as a sin offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 9's answer with a case of a required offering that is one bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said no required offering is a single bird. The יולדת is required to bring a חטאת, and it is just one bird. That seems to break Step 9's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth
A young pigeon
A sin offering

phrases.english: But there is the woman after childbirth,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַתְיָא בֶּן יוֹנָה אוֹ תוֹר לְחַטָּאת!
phrases.english: who brings a young pigeon or a dove as a sin offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim 'חובה מיהא לא אשכחן' from Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יולדת's חטאת is required and is only one bird, so a required single-bird offering does exist.

steps.title: Answer: the יולדת also brings a lamb
steps.stepSummary: The יולדת's bird is not her whole offering, because she brings a lamb with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is different, because there is a lamb together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 10 and closes this back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יולדת brings a lamb as an עולה together with her bird חטאת. So her single bird is only part of a larger set of offerings and is not a complete offering by itself. A גר who brought one bird alone would be bringing a one-bird offering, which is never found.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb
With it, alongside it

steps.whatToRemember: A גר who chooses birds must bring a pair, because the Torah never has a required offering made of a single bird standing alone.

phrases.english: Because there is a lamb with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by showing that the יולדת's bird is not a stand-alone offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יולדת's single bird seemed to be a required one-bird offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her bird comes together with a lamb, so it is not a one-bird offering by itself.

steps.title: Back to רבי: finding a source for מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי's statement that our ancestors entered the ברית through מילה, טבילה, and sprinkling of blood. It brings two verses for מילה and is setting up a question about the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through these things. Circumcision we can understand, since it is written that all the people who left Egypt were circumcised. Or we can learn it from the verse 'In your blood, live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main statement from Step 6 and starts checking its sources. Saying 'מילה is fine' is a setup. The next step also grants the sprinkling of blood, and then asks where טבילה comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא grants some parts so that the גמרא can then question another part. מילה is proven from יהושע, or from the doubled 'בדמיך' in יחזקאל. Blood is also granted next, and the real question is about טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is understandable (sets up a question on another part)
Circumcision
The covenant with ה׳
Alternatively

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not end the discussion. It agrees about מילה only to set up a question on the other requirements, which comes next.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַבְּרִית אֶלָּא כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Just as your ancestors entered the covenant only etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points back to רבי's list in Step 6: מילה, טבילה, and sprinkling of blood.

phrases.english: Granted, circumcision,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי מוּלִים הָיוּ כׇּל הָעָם הַיּוֹצְאִים״,

phrases.english: Alternatively, from here:
"And I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:6

phrases.english: and I said to you: In your blood, live, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מָה אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַבְּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about one bird and returns to רבי's main claim in Step 6 to find its sources.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we see that our ancestors entered the ברית through each of the three steps? This step grants מילה and sets up the question on the rest.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For מילה: יהושע 5:5, or the 'בדמיך' verse in יחזקאל 16:6.

steps.title: Blood is clear, but where is immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the 'granted' list by giving a verse for the blood. Then it asks where we learn טבילה from.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the sprinkling of blood is learned from the verse 'And he sent the young men of the children of Israel.' But immersion, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that מילה and blood both have clear verses. Now it asks where we learn that טבילה was part of entering the ברית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the young men leads into the offerings at הר סיני, so the blood step has a clear source. No verse openly mentions טבילה, so the גמרא needs to find one.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the blood of offerings so they are accepted
Immersion in a מקוה
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: [and] the bringing of blood, as it is written:
"And he sent the young men of the children of Israel."
phrases.notes: שמות 24:5. The verse goes on to say they brought עולות and שלמים.

phrases.english: But immersion, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'granted' setup from step 12 and asks for the missing source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse showing that טבילה was part of entering the ברית at הר סיני.

steps.title: Sprinkling blood on the people proves immersion
steps.stepSummary: משה sprinkled blood on the people, and sprinkling always requires טבילה first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And משה took half the blood and sprinkled it on the people.' And there is no sprinkling without immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by proving טבילה from the fact that blood was sprinkled on the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not mention טבילה directly. The גמרא uses a known rule: whoever has blood sprinkled on him must immerse first. So the people must have immersed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling
And he threw or sprinkled the blood

steps.whatToRemember: All three steps of entering the ברית now have sources: מילה, blood (the offerings at סיני), and טבילה (because there is no sprinkling without immersion).

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Moses took half the blood
and sprinkled it on the people"
and there is no sprinkling without immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood was sprinkled on the people, and sprinkling requires טבילה first, so the people immersed.

steps.title: Then how can we accept converts today?
steps.stepSummary: If entering the ברית needs a קרבן, then today, with no קרבנות, we could not accept גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, nowadays, when there are no offerings, we should not accept converts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with what was just said: a גר today cannot bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גר enters the same way our ancestors did, he needs all three steps, including the blood of a קרבן. Without the בית המקדש that step is impossible, so it seems no one could convert today.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if that is so (introduces a problem that follows from what was said)
Nowadays
Converts

phrases.english: But if so, now,
nowadays, when there is no offering,
we should not accept converts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling result from the three-step model just proven.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a גר needs a קרבן to enter the ברית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Today a קרבן is impossible, so conversion would be impossible too, and that cannot be right.

steps.title: A verse says converts are accepted in every generation
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a פסוק showing that גרים are accepted in all generations, even without קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: 'And if a stranger lives with you, or whoever is among you,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the problem with a פסוק about גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse continues 'throughout your generations,' so the Torah expects גרים in every era, including times with no בית המקדש. Being unable to bring the קרבן does not stop a person from becoming a גר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he lives (with you), said of a stranger
And so on (the rest of the verse)

steps.whatToRemember: A גר can be accepted today even though he cannot bring his קרבן.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
"And if a stranger lives with you
or whoever is among you," and so on.
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:14. The key words are in the 'and so on': 'throughout your generations.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Verse proving that the rule holds in all generations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a קרבן, conversion is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah accepts גרים in every generation, even when the קרבן cannot be brought.

steps.title: A convert today sets aside money for his birds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a גר today must set aside a quarter dinar toward his bird offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A convert nowadays must set aside a quarter dinar for his pair of birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about what a גר should do today about the קרבן he cannot bring yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is accepted without the קרבן, but the ברייתא says he must still prepare for it. He sets aside money now so he can buy the birds when the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
A quarter (of a dinar)
A pair of birds brought as an offering
That he set aside (designate)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A convert nowadays

phrases.notes: A quarter dinar, saved so he can buy the birds once the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from accepting גרים today to what a גר today must do about his קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר today must set aside a quarter dinar for his bird offering.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: this was cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reports that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי took a vote and cancelled this practice because of the risk of a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי already took a vote on it and cancelled it, because of the risk of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the ברייתא and says the practice of setting money aside was cancelled long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money set aside for a קרבן becomes holy. Since the בית המקדש might not be rebuilt for a long time, someone could easily use that money by mistake and misuse holy property. To prevent that, the practice was cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Took a vote (counted opinions)
Cancelled it
A mishap, a mistake that leads to sin

steps.confusionAlert: The reason given, the risk of misusing holy money, is about money set aside now. The גמרא does not say the גר's קרבן itself was cancelled, only the practice of setting money aside.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
already took a vote on it
phrases.notes: Some versions say עָלָיו, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is עָלֶיהָ. Either way it means 'on it.'

phrases.english: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, and he cancelled it,
because of the mishap.
phrases.notes: The worry is that someone would use the holy money by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting aside money for a גר's birds was cancelled by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי because of the risk of misusing holy money.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rules like רבי שמעון: a גר today does not set aside money for his birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר גרשום said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides the argument: we follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a גר today does not set aside a quarter dinar for his קן. The fear of misusing holy money decides the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: A גר today does not set aside money for his bird offering. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Gershom said
that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the ברייתא's first view and רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: a גר today does not set aside money for his קן.

steps.title: Another version places the ruling on a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling about a different ברייתא: a גר תושב may do מלאכה for himself on שבת, the way a Jew works on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach this ruling about this case, as the Rabbis taught: A גר תושב may do work on שבת for himself, like a Jew on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version, in which 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון' was said about a different ברייתא. It starts quoting that ברייתא, setting up רבי שמעון's view there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling has nothing to do with the גר's birds. It belongs to a ברייתא about a גר תושב on שבת. The first view there allows him the kind of work a Jew may do on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it (this statement) about another case
A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who keeps the seven Noahide מצוות
Work forbidden on שבת
The intermediate days of a festival (חול המועד)

steps.confusionAlert: A גר תושב is not a full convert. He is a non-Jew who accepted the seven Noahide מצוות, so this is a different person from the גר discussed until now.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it about this:
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling, 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.'

A ger toshav is permitted

steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view of the ברייתא: a גר תושב may do מלאכה for himself on שבת, the way a Jew may on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: like a Jew on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a גר תושב may work on שבת only the way a Jew may work on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: like a Jew on a Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 20 continues with a second opinion. רבי עקיבא says a גר תושב may work on שבת the way a Jew works on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion compared the גר תושב to a Jew on חול המועד. רבי עקיבא is stricter. On יום טוב a Jew may only do work needed for food, so the גר תושב gets only that much.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who lives in the Land and accepts the seven מצוות of בני נח
A Festival day, when only work needed for food is allowed

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Like a Jew on a Festival.
phrases.notes: He means the גר תושב may work on שבת the same way a Jew may on יום טוב, which is mainly for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in the ברייתא brought in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר תושב may do on שבת only the work a Jew may do on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: like a Jew on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a גר תושב may do any work for himself on שבת, just like a Jew on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A גר תושב does work on שבת for himself like a Jew on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the same ברייתא. רבי יוסי is the most lenient so far: for his own needs, a גר תושב may work freely on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From strictest to most lenient, the views are: like יום טוב (רבי עקיבא), like חול המועד (the first opinion), and like a regular weekday (רבי יוסי). For רבי יוסי there is no limit at all, as long as the work is for the גר תושב himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular weekday
For himself, for his own needs

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: A ger toshav
does work on Shabbat for himself
like a Jew on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third opinion in the same ברייתא, more lenient than רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר תושב may do any work for himself on שבת, like a Jew on a weekday.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: resident slaves too, like a weekday
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says both a גר תושב and resident male and female slaves may work for themselves on שבת like a Jew on a weekday. In this version, this is the opinion רב אדא בר אהבה rules like.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Both a גר תושב and a resident male and female slave do labor on שבת for themselves like a Jew on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The last opinion in the ברייתא. רבי שמעון agrees with the weekday standard and applies it to resident slaves as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון adds a new group: עבד ואמה התושבים get the same freedom as the גר תושב. Step 20 said some teach רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling on this ברייתא, so this is the opinion he rules like.

keyTerms.meaning: Resident male and female slaves who are not fully Jewish
A type of work that is forbidden on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Four views on a גר תושב on שבת: like יום טוב (רבי עקיבא), like חול המועד (first opinion), like a weekday (רבי יוסי), and like a weekday including resident slaves (רבי שמעון). In this version the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Both a ger toshav
and a resident male and female slave
do labor on Shabbat for themselves
like a Jew on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב וְאֶחָד עֶבֶד וְאָמָה הַתּוֹשָׁבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final opinion in the ברייתא; the one רב אדא בר אהבה rules like, according to the second version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר תושב and resident slaves may do work for themselves on שבת like a Jew on a weekday.

steps.title: New משנה: four cases where intentional is like unwitting
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four cases where a person brings a קרבן for a sin done on purpose, just as for a sin done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These bring an offering for an intentional sin just as for an unwitting one: one who has relations with a maidservant, a נזיר who became impure, the oath of testimony, and the oath on a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. Usually a קרבן is brought only for a mistake, but here are four cases where even a deliberate sinner brings one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is that קרבנות atone for שוגג, not מזיד. This משנה names exceptions where the קרבן is brought either way: שפחה חרופה, a נזיר who became טמא, a false שבועת העדות, and a false שבועת הפקדון.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin done on purpose
A sin done by mistake
Here, a שפחה חרופה: a maidservant betrothed to a Jewish slave; relations with her require an אשם
A false oath denying that one knows testimony
A false oath denying that one holds someone else's deposit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that all קרבנות can be brought for deliberate sins. These four are exceptions; the general rule is still that a קרבן חטאת is only for שוגג.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These bring
for an intentional sin as for an unwitting one:
one who has relations with a maidservant,
phrases.notes: This is the betrothed maidservant from ויקרא 19:20–22.

and the oath of testimony,
and the oath on a deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה; not connected to the גר discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these four cases, a קרבן is brought for a deliberate sin just as for an unwitting one.

steps.title: Five bring one offering for many sins, five bring a sliding-scale offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה introduces two lists of five. It then starts the first list: one who has relations with a שפחה many times, and a נזיר who became טמא many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five bring one offering for many transgressions, and five bring a sliding-scale offering. These bring one offering for many transgressions: one who has relations with a maidservant many times, and a נזיר who became impure many times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה announces two groups of five and begins listing the first group. These are people who bring only one קרבן even after repeating the sin many times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally each separate sin needs its own קרבן. Here the משנה says some people bring just one קרבן for many repeats of the same sin. It also mentions a second group who bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, an offering that depends on how much the sinner can afford.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliding-scale offering: animal, birds, or flour, depending on the sinner's wealth
Many transgressions, here meaning the same sin repeated
Many acts of relations
Many separate times of becoming impure

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with two new lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In certain cases, one קרבן covers many repetitions of the same sin.

steps.title: גמרא asks the source for the maidservant case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that one who has relations with a שפחה brings a קרבן even when he sinned on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One who has relations with the maidservant, from where do we derive it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking for a source for its first case. This is a setup question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the person with a שפחה brings a קרבן even for a deliberate sin. That goes against the usual rule, so the גמרא wants a פסוק that shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? A request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: One who has relations with the maidservant,
from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He is asking for the source that this sinner brings a קרבן even when he sinned on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with the first case listed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that relations with a שפחה חרופה require a קרבן even when done deliberately.

steps.title: Source for the שפחה case: the extra words in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the words אשר חטא, which appear twice in the פסוק of the אשם שפחה חרופה. The first time teaches that one קרבן covers many sins. The second time teaches that שוגג is treated like מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And the כהן shall atone for him with the ram of the אשם for his sin that he sinned." This teaches that he brings one קרבן for many sins. Later the פסוק says: "With the ram of the אשם... and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he sinned." That second mention makes the mistaken sin and the deliberate sin the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 26 by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from the פסוק itself that the אשם for a שפחה חרופה is brought even for a deliberate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אשר חטא appear twice in ויקרא 19:22, so each one must teach something. The first one teaches that a single קרבן covers many acts with the שפחה, which matches the first list in our משנה. The second one teaches that שוגג and מזיד are equal, so he brings the אשם either way.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram brought as a guilt offering (here, for a שפחה חרופה)
Many transgressions
A sin done by mistake
A sin done on purpose
To treat the mistaken sin the same as the deliberate one

steps.confusionAlert: Normally a קרבן is brought only for a sin done by mistake. Here the ברייתא says 'לעשות שוגג כמזיד': the אשם is the same whether he sinned by mistake or on purpose.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second אשר חטא in ויקרא 19:22 teaches that שוגג is like מזיד for the אשם שפחה חרופה. The first one teaches that one קרבן covers many sins.

steps.title: Asking the source for the נזיר who became טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and asks where we learn that a נזיר who became טמא on purpose brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who became impure: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second case in the משנה's list and asks for its source. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a נזיר who became טמא brings his קרבנות even if he did it on purpose. Since קרבנות are normally only for mistakes, the גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became ritually impure, usually through a dead body
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A nazirite who became impure,
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the שפחה case, the גמרא opens the same question for the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נזיר who became טמא on purpose still brings a קרבן.

steps.title: Learning from בפתע פתאום: mistake and beyond control
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a נזיר uses two words, פתע and פתאום. פתע means a mistake, as in the פסוק about accidental killing. פתאום means something beyond his control, as in ה׳ calling to משה suddenly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And if someone dies beside him unexpectedly, suddenly." "Unexpectedly" means by mistake, as the Torah says: "But if he pushed him unexpectedly without hatred." "Suddenly" means beyond his control, as the Torah says: "And ה׳ said suddenly to משה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק of נזיר, which uses two similar words. It explains each word by comparing it to another פסוק where that word appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have used one word, so each word adds a case. פתע is compared to the accidental killer, who acted without hatred, so it means שוגג. פתאום is compared to ה׳ calling משה, אהרן and מרים suddenly, which they could not control, so it means אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Unexpectedly; read here as a mistake (שוגג)
Suddenly; read here as beyond one's control
A situation beyond a person's control
And similarly it says (bringing another פסוק that uses the same word)

"And if someone dies beside him

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words בפתע פתאום in במדבר 6:9 include more than one kind of case: פתע is שוגג and פתאום is אונס.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: פתאום means on purpose
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא explains פתאום differently. It means a deliberate sin, because in משלי the פתאים, the fools, are punished, and punishment comes for what is done on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "Suddenly" means on purpose, as the פסוק says: "A clever man sees evil and hides, but the fools pass on and are punished."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that reads the word פתאום as a deliberate sin. This reading fits the משנה directly: a נזיר who became טמא on purpose also brings the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא links פתאום to פתאים, fools, in משלי 22:3. Those fools are punished, which shows they acted on purpose. So the פסוק of נזיר includes מזיד, and that is the source the גמרא was looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: Foolish or careless people; linked here to the word פתאום
And they are punished

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases have a source: for the שפחה, the extra אשר חטא makes שוגג like מזיד. For the נזיר, בפתע פתאום covers more than one kind of case, and the second ברייתא reads פתאום directly as מזיד.

"A clever man sees evil and hides himself,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פתאום in the פסוק of נזיר means a deliberate act, based on פתאים in משלי 22:3. So a נזיר who became טמא on purpose also brings a קרבן.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need the word פתע at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the double wording. פתאום alone can mean שוגג, מזיד, and אונס, so the word פתע seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק just write 'פתאום', since that word can mean by mistake, on purpose, and beyond his control. On purpose and beyond control we already showed. It also means by mistake, because it says 'the פתי believes every word.' So let the פסוק not write 'פתע'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the two-word reading from the last steps. If פתאום can cover all three kinds of sin, why does the Torah also write פתע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות in steps 29-30 showed that פתאום can mean אונס or מזיד. Here the גמרא adds a third meaning: a פתי, a naive person, believes whatever he hears, so he sins by mistake (שוגג). If one word covers everything, the second word looks pointless.

steps.kashyaTarget: The need for two separate words, פתע and פתאום, in the פסוק of the נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פתאום alone means שוגג, מזיד, and אונס, then פתע adds nothing.

steps.title: Without פתע we would limit the קרבן to a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if only פתאום were written, we would assume the קרבן is only for שוגג, as everywhere else in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had written only 'פתאום', which means by mistake, on purpose, and beyond control, I would have said: when he brings a קרבן, it is for a mistake, just like the whole Torah. But for beyond control or on purpose, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It shows what we would have wrongly thought if the Torah had written only פתאום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word with three possible meanings is unclear. We would read it the normal way: across the Torah a קרבן comes for שוגג. So we would leave out מזיד and אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an early mistaken idea)
Just as it is with, the same as
A sin done by mistake

phrases.english: If the verse had written "suddenly,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַשְׁמַע שׁוֹגֵג וּמַשְׁמַע מֵזִיד וּמַשְׁמַע אוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: which means by mistake, and means on purpose, and means beyond control,
I would have said:
when he brings an offering, it is for a mistake,
just as it is for the whole Torah,
phrases.notes: Everywhere else, a sin offering comes only for a sin done by mistake.

phrases.english: but for beyond control or on purpose, I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows what we would wrongly conclude without the extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only פתאום, the קרבן would apply only to שוגג, like the rest of the Torah
steps.terutzMaskana: Completed in the next step: פתע is needed so that פתאום teaches מזיד and אונס

steps.title: פתע covers mistakes, so פתאום must mean on purpose and beyond control
steps.stepSummary: The Torah wrote פתע for שוגג. That shows פתאום is teaching אונס and מזיד, and the נזיר brings a קרבן even for those.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the Merciful One wrote 'פתע', which means a mistake. This shows that 'פתאום' means beyond control and on purpose, and even so the Merciful One made him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. Since פתע already covers mistakes, פתאום must be teaching on purpose and beyond control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once פתע takes care of שוגג, we cannot read פתאום as only שוגג too. It must be adding something new: מזיד and אונס. This proves the משנה's rule that a נזיר who became טמא on purpose brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah
To reveal, to make clear
A sin done on purpose

steps.whatToRemember: פתע = שוגג. Because פתע covers mistakes, פתאום must mean מזיד and אונס. So a נזיר brings his קרבן even when he became טמא on purpose or beyond his control.

phrases.english: The Merciful One wrote "unexpectedly,"
which means a mistake,
to reveal about "suddenly"
that it means beyond control and on purpose,
and that even so, the Merciful One made him liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 32 and closes the topic of the נזיר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פתע teaches שוגג, so פתאום teaches מזיד and אונס. A נזיר who became טמא in any of these ways brings a קרבן.

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for a false שבועת העדות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and asks for the source that someone who swears a false שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The oath of testimony: from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It now asks for the source of the next case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed cases where a person brings a קרבן even for a sin done on purpose. After שפחה חרופה and the נזיר, the גמרא now looks for the source for a witness who falsely swears he knows no testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath by a witness that he knows no testimony
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The oath of testimony: from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know a false oath like this needs a קרבן even when sworn on purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as steps 26 and 28, now for the next case in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a false שבועת העדות requires a קרבן even when sworn on purpose

steps.title: The missing word ונעלם teaches that on purpose is liable too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the other cases of the sliding-scale קרבן say ונעלם, but שבועת העדות does not. That missing word teaches he is liable both by mistake and on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: In all of them it says 'and it was hidden'. Here it does not say 'and it was hidden'. This is to make him liable for a mistake just as for on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It compares the wording of the שבועת העדות פסוק with the פסוקים next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it was hidden from him' describe forgetting, which means a mistake. The other cases in that section say ונעלם, so they need a mistake. The שבועת העדות פסוק leaves it out, so he brings the קרבן in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was hidden from him; a sign the sin was by mistake
The sliding-scale offering, which depends on what the sinner can afford
To make liable

steps.whatToRemember: The other sliding-scale cases say ונעלם, so they apply only to a mistake. שבועת העדות leaves out ונעלם, so the witness brings a קרבן whether he swore falsely by mistake or on purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'שוגג כמזיד' can sound backwards. The point is that both are treated the same, so a witness who swore falsely on purpose also brings the קרבן.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
In all of them it says "and it was hidden,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2-4. "All of them" means the other cases that bring the sliding-scale קרבן.

phrases.english: here it does not say "and it was hidden"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1, the פסוק about שבועת העדות.

phrases.english: to make him liable for a mistake just as for on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ונעלם is missing from the שבועת העדות פסוק, so the witness is liable whether he swore falsely by mistake or on purpose.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the false deposit oath brings a קרבן even on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that someone who swears falsely about a deposit brings a קרבן even when he did it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The oath about a deposit: where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, שבועת הפקדון, and asks how we know it gets a קרבן even when done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן is only for a sin done by mistake. The משנה said שבועת הפקדון is different, so the גמרא wants a source, just as it found one for שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath where someone falsely denies holding another person's deposit or money
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The oath about a deposit, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: The question is how we know he brings a קרבן even when he swore falsely on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding the source for שבועת העדות, the גמרא asks the same question about the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that שבועת הפקדון requires a קרבן even for מזיד.

steps.title: Learned from the oath of testimony through the shared word 'shall sin'
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned through a גזרה שוה: the word תחטא appears in both שבועת הפקדון and שבועת העדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the word 'shall sin' here and the word 'shall sin' in the oath of testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we connect שבועת הפקדון to שבועת העדות because the Torah uses the same word, תחטא, for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the step before, we learned that שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even for מזיד. Because both sections share the word תחטא, the same rule carries over to שבועת הפקדון.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both places
'Shall sin', the word found in both sections
He learns it, he derives it

steps.whatToRemember: שבועת הפקדון brings a קרבן even for מזיד, learned from שבועת העדות through the shared word תחטא.

phrases.english: He learns 'shall sin', 'shall sin'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21 for the deposit, and ויקרא 5:1 for testimony.

phrases.english: from the oath of testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of תחטא/תחטא carries the מזיד rule from שבועת העדות over to שבועת הפקדון.

steps.title: Where do we learn one קרבן for many acts with a שפחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of five who bring one קרבן for many sins, and asks for the source for the one who was with a שפחה חרופה many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five people bring one offering for many sins. The משנה teaches: one who has relations with a maidservant many times. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new section of the משנה, the five cases where one קרבן covers many sins. It starts with the שפחה חרופה case and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually each sin needs its own קרבן. The משנה says that here one קרבן is enough even for many acts, so the גמרא wants to know where the Torah teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant who is half-freed and promised to a Jewish slave
One offering that covers many sins
Acts of relations

phrases.english: Five bring one offering
for many sins.
It teaches: one who has relations with the maidservant
phrases.notes: This is the שפחה חרופה, the maidservant promised to a Jewish slave.

phrases.english: many times. From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of a קרבן brought for מזיד and moves to the next list in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that one אשם covers many acts with a שפחה חרופה.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns two lessons from the words 'that he has sinned'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the verse about the שפחה חרופה's אשם. The first 'that he has sinned' teaches one קרבן for many sins, and the second teaches that מזיד is treated like שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'And the priest shall atone for him with the ram of the guilt offering for his sin that he has sinned.' This teaches that he brings one offering for many sins. 'With the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned': this treats on purpose like by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that finds the source in the extra words 'that he has sinned' in the verse about the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For his sin' would have been enough. The extra 'that he has sinned' shows that one אשם covers all the acts. The repeated phrase gives a second lesson: the ברייתא says it makes מזיד like שוגג, so either way he brings the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram brought as a guilt offering
'That he has sinned', the extra words the lessons come from
To treat a sin done on purpose like one done by mistake

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'And the priest shall atone for him with the ram of the guilt offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:22

phrases.english: for his sin that he has sinned',
this teaches that he brings one offering
for many sins.
'With the ram of the guilt offering
and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned'
to treat on purpose like by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38 and adds a second lesson about מזיד.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'that he has sinned' teaches one קרבן for many acts, and the repeated phrase makes the law the same for מזיד and שוגג.

steps.title: But the verse is already talking about a sin done on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the verse itself is about מזיד, so how can it be teaching that מזיד is like שוגג?
steps.simpleTranslation: But when this verse is written, it is written about one who sinned on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא's second lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need a verse to 'add' a case if the verse was not already about it. Since the verse about the שפחה חרופה is about מזיד from the start, the lesson 'treat מזיד like שוגג' makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: But the verse
It is written about one who sinned on purpose

phrases.english: But the verse, when it is written,
it is written about one who sinned on purpose!
phrases.notes: Earlier in that section, ויקרא 19:20 speaks of a punishment of lashes, and lashes are only given for a sin done on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קְרָא, כִּי כְּתִיב בְּמֵזִיד כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the ברייתא quoted in step 39.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse already deals with מזיד, so a lesson that adds מזיד to שוגג is backwards.

steps.title: Flip the wording: treat by mistake like on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording: the extra words teach that a שוגג is treated like a מזיד and also brings the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: to treat by mistake like on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by turning the ברייתא's words around, so they fit a verse that speaks about מזיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic verse is about מזיד. The extra 'that he has sinned' adds the שוגג case, so he brings the אשם either way. The final law is the same as before, but now the direction of the lesson is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say it this way (a fix to the wording)
To treat a sin done by mistake like one done on purpose

steps.whatToRemember: With a שפחה חרופה, one אשם covers many acts, and the אשם is brought both for מזיד and for שוגג. The verse is about מזיד, and the extra words add שוגג.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the verse starts with מזיד and adds שוגג. That is the opposite of most קרבנות, which are only for שוגג. Don't mix up the direction.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
to treat by mistake like on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 40 by reversing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the ברייתא (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the extra words add מזיד to a verse about שוגג.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is about מזיד, and the extra words add שוגג, so the אשם is brought in both cases.

steps.title: Five maidservants in one lapse: one קרבן or five?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא טירנאה asks רבי יוחנן whether a man who was with five different שפחות חרופות in one העלם brings one קרבן or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא of טירנא asked רבי יוחנן: If a man was with five espoused maidservants during one lapse of awareness, what is the law? Is he liable for each one, or only once?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. We just learned that many sins with one שפחה need only one קרבן, so now רבי חנינא asks what happens with five different women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that many acts with one שפחה חרופה need only one אשם. רבי חנינא asks whether that rule also joins together acts with five different women, when he never found out in between (one העלם).

keyTerms.meaning: A half-freed maidservant who is promised to a Jewish slave; being with her brings an אָשָׁם
One lapse of awareness: he never found out he sinned in between the acts
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טִירְנָאָה מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina of Tirna’a asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
One who is with five espoused maidservants
in one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable for each and every one,
or is he liable for only one?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טִירְנָאָה מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from many sins with one שפחה to sins with many different שפחות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether five different שפחות חרופות in one העלם need five קרבנות or one.

steps.title: He brings a קרבן for each woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he is liable for each one of the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: He is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a short, clear answer: five women means five קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the special 'one אשם for many times' rule from the משנה only covers one woman. Different women are counted separately, even in one lapse of awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable separately for each one

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: He said to him: He is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A separate אשם for each of the five שפחות.

steps.title: Why is this different from five lapses with one maidservant?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא challenges: the משנה says five separate lapses with one שפחה need only one קרבן, so why should five women in one lapse need five?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about this from five lapses of awareness with one maidservant?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא pushes back on the answer. He compares it to the משנה's case, where even five separate lapses with one שפחה need only one קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five separate lapses normally mean five קרבנות, yet with one שפחה the משנה says only one. If even that strong case gives one קרבן, it seems strange that one single lapse with five women should give five.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking why two cases are treated differently)
Lapses of awareness (more than one)

phrases.english: What is different from five lapses of awareness

phrases.english: with one maidservant?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵחֲמִשָּׁה הֶעְלֵמוֹת בְּשִׁפְחָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from step 43 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling of a קרבן for each woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If five lapses with one שפחה need only one קרבן, then one lapse with five שפחות should surely need only one too.

steps.title: Separate women are separate bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that one שפחה is one body, but five שפחות are five separate bodies (גופין מוחלקין).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One maidservant is not separate bodies; five maidservants are separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by pointing to what really splits the קרבנות here: different people, not different lapses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שפחה חרופה, the number of times or lapses does not matter, which is why one woman means one אשם. But each different woman is a separate 'body', and that does split the sin into separate קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate bodies: different people, which count as separate sins

steps.whatToRemember: With a שפחה חרופה: one woman = one אשם, no matter how many times or lapses. Different women = a separate אשם for each.

phrases.english: He said to him: One maidservant —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets here; the corrected wording moves it to the square brackets in the next line.

phrases.english: there are no separate bodies;
five maidservants are separate bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין שִׁפְחָה אַחַת גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 44.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five lapses with one woman is a stronger reason to split than one lapse with five women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lapses don't split the אשם of a שפחה, but separate bodies do.

steps.title: What is the source that separate bodies matter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asks where we learn that, for a שפחה, separate bodies require separate קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that with a maidservant, separate bodies count?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא accepts the idea but asks for a source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שפחה חרופה has its own unusual rules, it is not obvious that 'separate bodies' should matter here. He wants a פסוק that shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we learn it?
Regarding, in the case of

phrases.english: And from where do we know that regarding a maidservant
separate bodies count separately?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that separate women require separate קרבנות for a שפחה חרופה.

steps.title: The word 'אשה' appears for the שפחה too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reminds him that by עריות the word 'ואשה' teaches a separate קרבן for each woman, and the שפחה פסוק also says 'אשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you say regarding forbidden relations that 'And a woman' teaches to split for each woman? Regarding a maidservant it is also written: 'Whoever lies with a woman carnally...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a source: he uses a rule already known from עריות and shows the same word is in the שפחה פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 18:19 the word 'ואשה' teaches a separate חטאת for each woman. Since the שפחה חרופה פסוק also says 'אשה', the same idea of separate women applies there. The quote continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relations listed in the תורה
To split (to make each one a separate sin with its own קרבן)
Also

phrases.english: He said to him: Don't you say regarding forbidden relations
'And a woman' — to split for each and every woman?
